A lockpick is a rare and fragile tool used to open container locks. Most locks require more than one lockpick.
 
To use it, drag the lockpick onto a locked container or right-click the container. A lock can take up to 10 lockpicks total (100% combined effectiveness).

A professional locksmith's kit. Unfortunately, someone took all the lockpicks. Still, the special lock-turning tools are more convenient than ordinary screwdrivers.
 
%c[d_cyan] • %c[ui_gray_2] while in your inventory, reduce lock difficulty by 10%

A thin, protected metal folder for storing documents. While the X-labs were still operating, critical information and other data were placed in these folders and sent beyond the Zone of Exclusion. Such document folders are now nearly impossible to find in the Zone. Anyone would give anything to learn what's inside. The folder has a biometric lock that cannot be picked mechanically.\n \n

A heavy, richly decorated crate bearing the Monolith symbol on its lid. Supposedly made by the Wish Granter himself, these crates fulfil the Monolith's wishes for equipment and supplies. Ordinary lockpicks cannot open the lock; some gravitational anomaly holds the pins in place. Still, such a rare find is sure to attract traders or collectors.\n \n

A hard, waterproof case often used to transport long rifles. The only people in the Zone who can afford such luxury for their weapons are mercenaries or other equally dangerous types. Finding one is deeply unsettling.\n \n

A large wooden crate once used by local villagers to store hunting shotguns and surplus weapons from World War II. Some remain in villages around the Zone of Exclusion; stalkers reuse others to store their weapons. The wood is old and rotten, so breaking the lock with an axe won't be difficult.\n \n

A military crate with a padlock, usually used to transport weapons and ammunition. After the failed first attempts to explore the Zone of Exclusion, vast amounts of equipment, including crates like this, were abandoned. It's hard to say how long this one has been here; perhaps it has been in the Zone since it began. It's very heavy, so don't carry it around.\n \n

A professionally made lead container with an internal lock and the emblem of Ukraine's Ministry of Science. Ecologists often use such containers to carry artifacts through dangerous parts of the Zone. They block radioactive emissions exceptionally well and protect their contents from the elements and thieving stalkers. Even escorted ecologist groups are often robbed, so storing valuable information and artifacts in secure containers became standard practice. The internal lock is very complex and will be difficult to pick.\n \n

A medium-sized toolbox with a padlock. Such boxes are the cheapest way for a stalker to store personal belongings; they offer little protection against break-ins and are easy to open. Usually only green rookies dare to leave anything valuable inside. The padlock is very simple and can be picked with little effort.\n \n

A locked fireproof briefcase. Fairly light and portable. Scientists and the military usually use such cases to transport secret documents, while criminal organizations use them to carry large sums of money. As befits a case for such delicate cargo, its lock is quite secure.\n \n

A hard container with an internal lock. Its body is made of some kind of composite material and is quite resistant to rough handling. Such containers are ordered from the mainland and are popular with foreigners and wealthy stalkers as the best way to keep personal belongings safe. The internal lock is fairly complicated, but can still be picked.\n \n

A hard container with an internal lock. Its body is made of some kind of composite material and is quite resistant to rough handling. Such containers are ordered from the mainland and are popular with foreigners and wealthy stalkers as the best way to keep personal belongings safe. The internal lock is fairly complicated, but can still be picked.\n \n

A simple steel box with a padlock. Unlike a toolbox, it is designed to keep its contents secure and offers decent protection against break-ins. The padlock is good quality, though it won't be difficult to pick.\n \n

A locked, weatherproof box containing useful field supplies. Such discreet caches are mainly used by paramilitary groups and covert teams to restock their agents in the field. There are no markings on the outside, so it's hard to tell who owned it. It is usually secured with a sturdy lock that deters even the most resourceful thieves. It contains nothing exceptionally valuable, but food, medicine and ammunition are always useful.\n \n
The axe broke while opening the box.
A strange key. It looks as if it has passed through some kind of anomalous field. Its blade is unnaturally bent, and its teeth glow ominously, constantly changing shape and size.\n \n

A special device used to pick locks quickly. Its snap mechanism strikes all the lock pins at once, aligning them so the cylinder can turn. It is reliable and can open most simple locks with little effort, but it won't help with more complex ones.
